original_question: (Well-known problem). Does there exist a finitely presented group G such that G ≅ G × H for some non-trivial group H? The first finitely generated example was constructed in(J. M. Tyrer Jones, J. Austral. Math. Soc., 17(1974), 174–196). A finitely presented group that surjects onto its own direct square was constructed in(G. Baumslag, C. F. Miller, III, Bull. London Math. Soc., 20, no. 3(1988), 239–244).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.47 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": the exact official formulation is "Does there exist a finitely presented group G such that G ≅ G × H for some non-trivial group H?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost verbatim. It states the same existence problem, keeps the finitely presented hypothesis on G, uses the same isomorphism condition G ≅ G × H with H non-trivial, and includes exactly the two historical references that the paper itself gives immediately after the problem statement.
missing_details: The paper imposes no finiteness assumptions on H; it is only required to be a non-trivial group.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to say explicitly that ≅ means isomorphism of abstract groups and G × H is the direct product.
The Baumslag-Miller surjection onto the direct square is background only; it is not part of the question and should not replace the isomorphism problem.
The official target in the paper is the existence of a finitely presented self-product decomposition G ≅ G × H, not merely a finitely presented group mapping onto G × G.
refined_question: Does there exist a finitely presented group G such that, for some non-trivial group H (with no further assumptions on H), the group G is isomorphic to the direct product G × H?
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact problem recorded as 21.47 in the current arXiv version of 1401.0300. The paper states this problem in essentially the same words and then adds the Tyrer Jones finitely generated example and the Baumslag-Miller finitely presented surjection onto the direct square as context on the same page. Nothing nearby in the paper sharpens this into an explicitly equivalent reformulation, so the closest faithful rewrite is just the official question with the hidden point made explicit that H is arbitrary apart from being non-trivial. Because the paper's own wording is already sharp, the main refinement is only to make the isomorphism and direct-product notation completely stand-alone and to avoid drifting into the weaker surjection variant.
